Let \(P=\operatorname{diag}(p_1,\dots,p_n)\). If \(g=A_nx\), an exact coordinate step in coordinate \(i\) decreases the quadratic by
\[
f_n(x)-f_n(x^+)=\frac{g_i^2}{4},
\]
because \((A_n)_{ii}=2\). Hence
\[
\frac{\mathbb E[f_n(x^+)\mid x]}{f_n(x)}
=
1-\frac12\frac{x^TA_nPA_nx}{x^TA_nx}.
\]
So minimizing \(\Gamma_n(p)\) is equivalent to maximizing
\[
\mu(p):=\inf_{x\ne0}\frac{x^TA_nPA_nx}{x^TA_nx}.
\]

Put \(K=A_n^{-1}\), and write \(q=A_nx\). Then
\[
\mu(p)=\inf_{q\ne0}\frac{\sum_i p_iq_i^2}{q^TKq}.
\]
For every \(p\), testing \(q=(1,\dots,1)\) gives
\[
\mu(p)\le \frac{1}{\mathbf 1^TK\mathbf 1}.
\]

Now solve \(A_ns=\mathbf 1\). The solution is
\[
s_i=\frac{i(n+1-i)}2,
\]
so
\[
S:=\sum_{i=1}^n s_i=\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{12}.
\]
Thus every \(p\) satisfies
\[
\mu(p)\le \frac1S=\frac{12}{n(n+1)(n+2)}.
\]

Choose
\[
p_i^*=\frac{s_i}{S}
=
\frac{6i(n+1-i)}{n(n+1)(n+2)}.
\]
To see this attains the bound, note that \(K=A_n^{-1}\) has nonnegative entries and row sums \(s_i\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{diag}(s)-K\succeq0,
\]
because
\[
q^T(\operatorname{diag}(s)-K)q
=
\frac12\sum_{i,j}K_{ij}(q_i-q_j)^2\ge0.
\]
Therefore, for \(p=p^*\),
\[
\sum_i p_i^*q_i^2
=
\frac1S\sum_i s_iq_i^2
\ge
\frac1S q^TKq,
\]
so \(\mu(p^*)\ge 1/S\). Combined with the upper bound, \(\mu(p^*)=1/S\).

Uniqueness: if equality holds for some \(p\), then \(q=\mathbf1\) must be a minimizer of the Rayleigh quotient. The stationarity condition gives
\[
p=\frac{K\mathbf1}{\mathbf1^TK\mathbf1}=\frac{s}{S},
\]
so \(p=p^*\).

Finally,
\[
\Gamma_n^*
=
1-\frac12\mu(p^*)
=
1-\frac{6}{n(n+1)(n+2)}.
\]

\[
\boxed{
\left(
\left(\frac{6i(n+1-i)}{n(n+1)(n+2)}\right)_{i=1}^n,
\ 1-\frac{6}{n(n+1)(n+2)}
\right)
}
\]
